subject: Request: one-off rate waiver for SiloShift pilot expansion — VP/CFO sign-off
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-04-30 09:12 -0700
Subject: SiloShift pilot expansion — request for one-off rate waiver

Team,

Quick summary: SiloShift (existing pilot live with 10k tokens/day) is asking to expand scope to 3x usage immediately for a new product line they’re incubating. They’re pushing for a one-off commercial concession: 30% off list rates for the first 90 days of the expansion to remove procurement friction and secure a faster go-live.

Why this matters: this prospect is a strategic use case for our low-latency private offering and would be a strong reference in our dataplane story. They are willing to sign a convertible commercial addendum but procurement needs an explicit executive waiver to accept >20% deviation from our published starter package.

Ask: I need an executive (VP/CFO) sign-off memo to present to their procurement team by EOD Wednesday. Attached: commercial summary, a pricing model and a quick revenue impact calc.

Proposed guardrails I’d recommend if we approve:
- One-off 30% discount applied to first 90 days only
- 6-month minimum commitment afterward (standard T&Cs)
- Revenue protection clause (true-up if usage > forecast)

If we can’t do 30%, I’d accept a structured split: 25% first 30 days, 15% next 60 days, with an accelerated ramp milestone tied to payment terms.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
attach: SiloShift_Commercial_Summary.pdf, SiloShift_pricing_model.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-30 11:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: SiloShift pilot expansion — request for one-off rate waiver

Jordan — thanks for the context. A couple quick thoughts from GTM:

1) Value: SiloShift is high leverage as a reference in the private deployment/edge space. If the expansion lands, it unlocks two other inbound prospects.
2) Economics: 30% across 90 days is aggressive; the unit economics for the pilot expansion are marginal unless we cap the waived period.
3) Negotiation tactic: split the discount and require payment on signature for the first 30 days (prepay credits). That reduces our receivables risk and signals commitment.

My recommendation: Approve up to 25% but require either (a) 3 months prepayment for the discounted portion or (b) 30% only if they accept a 12-month minimum and a partial non-refundable onboarding fee.

I’ve added a short note in HubSpot and linked the updated pricing model: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/DS-2028-093 (see comment). If legal will OK the convertible addendum, we can accelerate.

Karthik
Director, Enterprise Sales

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-01 08:22 -07:00
Subject: Re: SiloShift pilot expansion — request for one-off rate waiver

Folks — reviewed the model (attached revenue_impact_v2.xlsx). Short form: approving 30% for 90 days reduces near-term ARR recognition but can be mitigated by term/commitment language. Key points:

- If we push the commitment to 12 months (start date = end of 90-day discount window), net present value keeps within acceptable thresholds for enterprise pilots.
- Legal needs a standard revenue protection clause: customer to true-up if usage outpaces forecast by >40% during the discount window.
- Ops: require pinned model version and SLA 2 during the discounted window. This prevents silent degradation risk.

Recommended approval path for exec memo to procurement:
1) Approve 30% one-off discount for first 45 days only (compromise), OR
2) Approve 25% for 90 days subject to (a) 6-month minimum AND (b) 30% of the discounted value pre-paid on signature.

I’ve attached a draft memo template that legal can sign off on if we pick an option.

Marissa Cole
Head, Commercial Operations
attach: revenue_impact_v2.xlsx

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-02 13:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: SiloShift pilot expansion — request for one-off rate waiver

Looping in Markus for CFO perspective. High-level finance read:

- Baseline: our blended unit margin for this customer at list is ~55%. A 30% list discount applied for 90 days drops margin below 30% for that period if usage spikes.
- Required mitigations to preserve overall economics: either prepayment (preferred) or a non-refundable onboarding fee + true-up.
- If we structure as 25% discount for 90 days with a 6-month minimum and a 30% prepayment on the discounted bucket, expected revenue impact is acceptable and recoverable.

Markus — can you weigh in with sign-off language? We need an explicit yes/no and any additional conditions (escrow, payment cadence) we require before Jordan sends the executive memo to SiloShift procurement.

Naomi
Head of FP&A

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-02 15:08 -07:00
Subject: Re: SiloShift pilot expansion — request for one-off rate waiver

Thanks for all the diligence. Executive position: APPROVE conditional one-off concession. Terms required for CFO sign-off:

1) Discount: 25% off list rates applied to the expanded usage for up to 90 days.
2) Commitment: 6-month minimum starting at the end of the discount window. If they decline, discount is void.
3) Payment: Customer must prepay 50% of the discounted-period invoice at signature; remaining 50% due net 30.
4) Revenue protection: true-up if actual usage exceeds forecast by >30% during the discount window (customer liability).
5) Legal & Ops: model pinning and SLA level confirmed in addendum; we require a pre-signed addendum before any cutover.

If Jordan can get SiloShift to agree to the above, I’ll sign the memo and copy the procurement team. Send me the final one-page executive memo and I’ll provide a formal sign-off by EOD.

Markus Klein
VP Finance (interim CFO)

On Thu, May 02, 2028 at 15:09 Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Markus — I will draft the one-page memo with the terms and loop legal. I’ll share the memo link here for final sign-off.
>
> Jordan
> Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
